narrative: context/problem → Navier solution → how it works and where it fits → bounded demonstration and pilot → evidence-led scale → partnership ask
claim_status_rule: Verified facts may be stated. Company-reported metrics are labeled. Candidates and future paths remain visibly qualified. Unsupported values and bindings remain null.

slide_source_map.title: WETA × Navier — a new electric ferry layer for the San Francisco Bay
slide_source_map.guidance: Passenger-service proposition and Alameda presence; no WETA commitment, procurement, route, funding or deployment claim.

slide_source_map.title: The proposition — give WETA another way to grow service
slide_source_map.guidance: Executive public-transit proposition: cost path, reach, rider experience and Bay-native support.

slide_source_map.title: The Bay needs more ferry service — not every trip needs the same ferry
slide_source_map.guidance: Official WETA planning context and the right-sizing problem; no corridor economics or demand claim.

slide_source_map.title: The N30 — a small ferry that flies above the waves
slide_source_map.guidance: Plain-English N30 vehicle explanation using Navier company materials; capability subject to certification and WETA review.

slide_source_map.title: Why the cost to serve can fall
slide_source_map.guidance: Company-reported energy proof point and operating-cost logic; route-specific economics remain unvalidated.

slide_source_map.title: The passenger experience — a calmer, quieter public-transit trip
slide_source_map.guidance: Passenger benefits are described as product intent; accessibility and public-service requirements remain joint design gates.

slide_source_map.title: A platform, not a one-boat answer
slide_source_map.guidance: N30 is the current starting point; larger-capacity and autonomy paths are future possibilities, not commitments.

slide_source_map.title: One network — three practical uses
slide_source_map.guidance: Three conceptual WETA uses; WETA retains network, safety, procurement and public-service authority.

slide_source_map.title: Start with markets WETA already knows
slide_source_map.guidance: Mission Bay, Treasure Island and Redwood City are WETA-published planning areas; Alameda/Oakland is a local screening context. No route commitment.

slide_source_map.title: First — a Bay demonstration from Alameda
slide_source_map.guidance: Bounded evidence-building demonstration from Alameda; output is an evidence pack, not a route or procurement decision.

slide_source_map.title: Then — a WETA-selected service pilot
slide_source_map.guidance: One WETA-selected pilot only after certification, accessibility, terminal, charging, labor and procurement requirements.

slide_source_map.title: When the data supports it — build a new electric service layer
slide_source_map.guidance: Scale only after Bay evidence and WETA approval; autonomy remains a future regulated pathway.

slide_source_map.title: Six gates. No shortcuts.
slide_source_map.guidance: Service gates prevent unsupported readiness claims.

slide_source_map.title: How the partnership works
slide_source_map.guidance: Roles and governance for a possible partnership; no binding commitment.

slide_source_map.title: Next step — choose one Bay problem
slide_source_map.guidance: Working-session ask only; no outreach sent and no approval implied.
